subject.title: [Feature]: Multi-role support in Chat UI for multi-agent workflows

question: Should OpenClaw add a durable per-message sender identity contract for multi-agent conversations, and what canonical fields and trust rules should flow through Gateway schemas, transcripts, live/history events, and Control UI rendering?
rationale: The missing behavior is source-visible, but the fix chooses a cross-surface public API and persistence contract rather than a narrow renderer repair; automation should not choose permanent identity semantics alone.

options.title: Add Durable Sender Identity
options.body: Adopt an additive sender object with id, kind, display name, source session or agent, and render metadata, then migrate the affected protocol, transcript, event, and UI paths together.

options.title: Keep SenderLabel Projection Only
options.body: Treat current `senderLabel` and provenance projection as the intended scope, leaving only narrower requester-name or blank-label defects to their own issues.

options.title: Defer To Narrow Bugs
options.body: Let the requester-name and WebChat fallback issues handle immediate gaps while accepting that durable audit identity remains intentionally unowned for now.

recommendation.title: Add Durable Sender Identity
recommendation.body: Adopt an additive sender object with id, kind, display name, source session or agent, and render metadata, then migrate the affected protocol, transcript, event, and UI paths together.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is the inter-session provenance/session API work and prior review of this exact boundary.
